request.recipient: Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting as Article II.7.5 administrator at withdrawal, with a later target transition to a dOSPO 501(c)(3) subject to governance.
request.what: Establish a one-year independent Cardano dOSPO and Open Maintenance Framework program to coordinate and sustain open source infrastructure through operations, advisory councils, maintenance funding, maintainer development, bounties, and ecosystem activation.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 4,094,000 ADA over 12 months for a revised Cardano dOSPO and OMF program.
Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting is designated as the sole Article II.7.5 administrator at the moment of treasury withdrawal, with final allocation authority during the period.
Mill Law Firm is designated as independent financial auditor on a quarterly cadence through month 12.
The proposal says a 501(c)(3) public charity legal entity is in progress and targeted to be operational by month 6, but initial capital is needed to complete establishment.
The program would use two advisory councils whose feedback is published before disbursements, while the administrator retains final allocation authority.

The Maintenance Fund would deploy 2,000,000 ADA over 12 months to support high-risk Cardano open source infrastructure selected through dependency audits, centrality scores, bus factor assessments, and published rubrics.
The proposal claims selection follows published dependency centrality data rather than relationships and that public quarterly reporting will cover all programs.

The proposer claims prior experience as Senior Manager of Open Source Governance and Head of OSPO at Intersect, including building Cardano open source governance functions and shaping the Paid Open Source Model.

The proposal targets 15 or more high-centrality projects funded by month 12, 40% top-50 dependency coverage, 100% quarterly report publication, and bus factor 2+ for all targeted top-20 centrality projects.

The proposer asserts that the model is decentralized, accountable to governance, and can be shut down or replaced through on-chain Info Actions, including a commitment to sponsor such an action if requested by 15 or more DReps.

summary: The document describes a 4,094,000 ADA, one-year treasury request for an independently administered Cardano dOSPO/OMF program led initially by Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting, with advisory councils, legal entity formation, quarterly audits and reports, and multiple open source sustainability programs centered on data-driven maintenance funding.
